summary: No public dataset holds decapod sperm imaged under a controlled osmotic series; repository searches (Zenodo, Dryad, DataCite, BioImage Archive, EMPIAR) return only taxonomic sperm-ultrastructure papers (hermit crabs, potamid crabs) and vertebrate/insect sperm image sets, and the Cell Image Library exposes no decapod sperm series. The variables the test needs — paired external osmolarity, cell volume and surface area — exist nowhere; they would have to be generated by new microscopy on Inachus, Galathea, Dromia or crayfish sperm in graded NaCl, KCl and sucrose solutions.
next_step: Design a new experiment: image fresh decapod sperm (e.g. Carcinus or crayfish) in a graded osmotic series of two salts with different molecular weight, record outlines, and deposit in BioImage Archive; literature ultrastructure papers can supply the 'normal form' reference only.
obstacles_confirmed: No public osmotic series exists for the named genera Inachus, Galathea, Dromia and crayfish.
Isolated micrographs of crustacean sperm lack the paired external concentration and surface-area measurements the test needs.
Public images rarely include controlled osmolarity metadata.
